title: Service Specification
description: Declarative description of a service to be scaffolded by `servicectl init`. A v2 spec is a self-contained JSON object; the same shape is accepted by `--from-config` and (when committed at the repo root) by `servicectl refresh` as the source of truth.

schema_version.description: Spec schema version. Must be 2 for this schema. Bump to a new top-level number when the shape changes incompatibly.

service.description: Identity and naming for the scaffolded service. Kept separate from runtime concerns so the same spec can be re-targeted at a different name (e.g. for staging clones).

name.description: Service name. Used for the output directory, the container image name, and (where applicable) the cloud resource name. Allowed: letters, digits, dash, underscore, dot.

description.description: Free-text one-liner used in the generated README and the scaffolder's success panel.

template.description: Runtime template to render. Determines language, framework, and the test/precommit toolchain that gets installed.

ci.description: CI provider configuration. Renders the workflow file and sets the runner expectations in the generated pre-commit hooks.

coverage_threshold.description: Minimum test coverage (percent) required for a green CI run and a passing local pre-commit. The pre-commit hook parses the same coverage output the CI does and fails the commit at the same threshold.

deploy.description: Deployment target. The `local` target skips cloud manifest generation; everything else emits a deploy overlay under `deploy/<target>/`.

gcp_project_id.description: GCP project ID for `deploy.target=gcp-*`. May be omitted at scaffold time; the rendered Terraform will refuse to apply until the placeholder is replaced.

registry.description: Container registry. Short aliases (`ghcr`, `dockerhub`) are expanded to hostnames (`ghcr.io`, `docker.io`) inside the image name.

database.description: Database backend. Each value maps to a specific cloud resource type and a local-dev Docker image. Pick the engine, not the cloud-specific flavor — `deploy.target` decides whether the Azure, GCP, or local Compose resource is emitted.

overlays.description: Composability layer. Each entry adds a feature on top of the bare template + deploy + db. Overlays are designed to be added, removed, and reordered without invalidating the rest of the spec. v1's flat flags (`--auth oauth`, `--otel`, `--elk`) are projected onto entries here; see the migration guide in `docs/spec-v2.md`.

auth.description: Authentication overlay. `none` emits no auth scaffolding; the others render middleware, env wiring, and a starter login route.

observability.description: Telemetry overlay. `none` ships no telemetry; `opentelemetry` adds OTel SDK + exporter wiring; the logs/ backends are orthogonal and listed under `logs`.

logs.description: Log shipping target. The OTel overlay must be enabled for log exporters to light up; this entry just chooses the destination.
